"""
Pytest test suite for match_parens function.
Generated via SMT/CSP constraint analysis covering boundary values,
equivalence classes, and counterexamples.
"""

from target import match_parens


# BOUNDARY CASES: Empty and single-character strings

def test_both_empty_strings():
    """BOUNDARY - Empty strings produce balanced result"""
    assert match_parens(["", ""]) == "Yes"


def test_empty_with_balanced():
    """BOUNDARY - Empty doesn't affect balanced string"""
    assert match_parens(["", "()"]) == "Yes"


def test_balanced_with_empty():
    """BOUNDARY - Order-independent when one string is empty"""
    assert match_parens(["()", ""]) == "Yes"


def test_empty_with_single_open():
    """BOUNDARY - Empty with single '(' results in imbalance"""
    assert match_parens(["", "("]) == "No"


def test_empty_with_single_close():
    """BOUNDARY - Empty with single ')' goes negative"""
    assert match_parens(["", ")"]) == "No"


def test_single_open_single_close():
    """BOUNDARY - Complementary single characters"""
    assert match_parens(["(", ")"]) == "Yes"


def test_single_close_single_open():
    """BOUNDARY - Reversed order requires correct sequencing"""
    assert match_parens([")", "("]) == "Yes"


def test_both_single_opens():
    """BOUNDARY - Two opens alone cannot balance"""
    assert match_parens(["(", "("]) == "No"


def test_both_single_closes():
    """BOUNDARY - Two closes go negative immediately"""
    assert match_parens([")", ")"]) == "No"


# EQUIVALENCE CLASSES: Multi-character patterns with internal balance

def test_two_opens_two_closes():
    """EQUIVALENCE CLASS - Multiple opens then closes balance"""
    assert match_parens(["((", "))"]) == "Yes"


def test_simple_balanced_concatenation():
    """EQUIVALENCE CLASS - Both individually balanced"""
    assert match_parens(["()", "()"]) == "Yes"


def test_nested_vs_flat_both_balanced():
    """EQUIVALENCE CLASS - Different nesting patterns both balance"""
    assert match_parens(["(())", "()()"]) == "Yes"


def test_longer_balanced_sequences():
    """EQUIVALENCE CLASS - Longer balanced components"""
    assert match_parens(["()()()", "()"]) == "Yes"


def test_example_from_docstring():
    """EQUIVALENCE CLASS - Provided example in docstring"""
    assert match_parens(["()(", ")"]) == "Yes"


def test_single_open_with_balanced_suffix():
    """EQUIVALENCE CLASS - Open count matches close count"""
    assert match_parens(["(", ")()"]) == "Yes"


# COUNTEREXAMPLES: Cases where naive validation would fail

def test_total_opens_exceed_closes():
    """COUNTEREXAMPLE - Imbalanced: 3 opens, 2 closes"""
    assert match_parens(["(((", "))"]) == "No"


def test_total_closes_exceed_opens():
    """COUNTEREXAMPLE - Imbalanced: 2 opens, 3 closes"""
    assert match_parens(["((", ")))"]) == "No"


def test_alternating_fails_both_orders():
    """COUNTEREXAMPLE - Inverted pattern fails both concatenation orders"""
    assert match_parens([")( ", "()"]) == "No"


def test_balanced_with_inverted_suffix():
    """COUNTEREXAMPLE - Balanced string paired with inverted suffix"""
    assert match_parens(["()", ")("]) == "No"


def test_balanced_with_single_unmatched_open():
    """COUNTEREXAMPLE - Total opens exceed closes by one"""
    assert match_parens(["()", "("]) == "No"
